title: Adam, the Senses, the Generations, and Divine Sorrow
summary: The natural man taken up in five teachings: how Saklas and his powers molded Adam and Eve as a counterfeit imprinted with the seal of the Ambassador's icon; how the body is built as a city of sense-storehouses with the heart-king and the Mind of Light arriving at the gates to take the keys; why the first generations lived enormously long while we live briefly, traced to the descent of governance from year to month to day to hour to moment; the three griefs of Mother of Life, First Man, and a third divine power over the bound Living Soul; and the four weepings of the garments of the First Man — three at the descent, one heavier at the consummation.
organizing_principle: A movement from Adam's molding through the body's interior architecture and the descent of the generations to divine compassion for what has been bound — closing on the irrevocable sorrow over souls who choose Darkness.
